Distinguished delegates, many of the vital initiatives I have highlighted are entirely dependent on extra-budgetary contributions. While space activities and related regulatory issues have dramatically scaled up, our resources continue to be disproportionately inadequate. Let me give you one example. In 2022, a time when forecasts projected 3,300 operational satellites in orbit by 2026, member states approved a P3 position for registration. This has generated a processing backlog currently standing at 4 months, and without additional resources, it will increase to 12 months by 2030 and even exceed a year if constellations deploy faster. This backlog creates legal and operational risks for member states. The lack of registration undermines crucial transparency obligations. It complicates liability attribution in the event of collision. No registration also complicates the identification of space debris at a time in which every year more and more member states request UNUSA assistance when debris lands on their territory, a trend that will increase and accelerate as congestion increases.
